To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the solutions to the consistency condition can be characterized by a set of integers, that these integers are the coefficients of a polynomial in the gauge coupling, and that the polynomial is uniquely determined up to a finite number of choices.

1) the solutions of the consistency conditions are in one to one correspondence with the solutions of the cohomological equations, 2) the solutions to the consistency condition are complete for compact gauge groups, 3) the solutions to cohomological equations are complete for any finite gauge group, 4) the solutions to all cohomological equations for any finite gauge groups are complete, 5) the solutions to any cohomological equation are complete if the gauge group is compact.

(i) the solutions to the consistency equations are complete, i.e., there are no other solutions, (ii) the solutions are nontrivial in the sense that they do not follow from a trivial solution, and (iii) the solutions are unique up to the action of a group, called the gauge group.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a systematic study of the anomalies in gauge theories.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no other anomalies than the ones known to us, at least for the case of compact gauge groups.
the known anomalies are all anomalies, that is, all anomalies are anomalies.
the known anomalies exhaust all possible ones, at least in the sense that all possible anomalies can be realized as anomalies of the gauge theory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the anomaly is a gauge-invariant quantity and that the anomaly cancellation is the necessary and sufficient condition for a consistent gauge theory.
all the solutions to the consistency equations can be written in the form of a sum of a renormalizable anomaly and an anomaly that can be absorbed in a redefinition of the fields.
we have shown how to construct the most general consistent anomaly free models with a given symmetry group, and we have shown that there are no anomalies in the case of compact groups.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the consistency conditions for the anomalies in the nonrenormalizable sector are the same as those in the renormalizable sector, but the solutions to these conditions are more complicated.
the consistency conditions for nonrenormalisable models can be formulated in terms of a simple and elegant mathematical object, the cohomology of a Lie algebra.
the anomaly cancellation conditions are not sufficient to fix all the parameters of the theory.
